review.title: Candidate failover policy
review.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. This task declared packages/contracts/** for a change that touches exactly two files in that package. pathsOverlap tests prefix containment in BOTH directions, so that wildcard prefix-contained PL-0706's single leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and made this task unclaimable for as long as a security corrective held one forty-line file. It was not alone: PL-0205, PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 all declared the same wildcard, so one leaf starved four P0 tasks across two lanes while claude-media sat idle and ai:dispatch correctly returned an empty wave. A reservation is supposed to name what a task writes; a package-wide wildcard names what its package contains, and the difference is a whole lane. The two entries below were derived by reading the implementation rather than guessed: domains/failover.ts declares playbackFailureKindSchema, PLAYBACK_FAILURE_KINDS, playbackAttemptFailureSchema and failoverPolicySchema under a header naming this task, and testing/arbitraries.ts carries playbackFailureKindArb and failoverPolicyArb. Both are prefix-disjoint from packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts in both directions. testing/arbitraries.ts is ALSO declared by PL-0205, deliberately, and the overlap is real rather than an oversight: both tasks genuinely wrote that file, and declaring it on one of them alone would understate one review surface to flatter the other. Being precise about what that costs, because two different rules are easy to conflate here: ai:validate ERRORS only on an active write-path conflict under DIFFERENT owners, so this shared entry never makes validate fail while both tasks share claude-media -- but conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner. Combined with claude-media's maxParallel, which was 1 when this was written and is 2 since round 40, that means exactly one of PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0206 can be active at a time, and packages/media-engine/** would have forced that anyway. packages/media-engine/** was initially left wide on the argument that this task, PL-0205 and PL-0206 all write across that package, share an owner, and would gain nothing from narrowing. That argument was later refused -- see the narrowing paragraph below -- and the wildcard is gone. THE IMPLEMENTATION PREDATES THE CLAIM, AND THIS TASK IS QUEUED BEHIND PL-0205 RATHER THAN RECONCILED WITH IT. packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts, packages/media-engine/src/scheduling.ts and failover.ts, four test suites, a dedicated vitest config and a bench script are all already in committed history under headers naming this task, while it was never claimed and carries no gate results -- so ai:start must not capture HEAD here either; it needs --reconcile-existing with a base derived from git, the first parent of the first commit reported by git rev-list --reverse HEAD over packages/contracts/src/domains/failover.ts. That contract module is the right probe rather than a media-engine file, because the engine package already existed for PL-0201 and PL-0202 and its earliest touch would open the range two tasks too early. IT COULD NOT BE DONE IN THE SAME ROUND AS PL-0205 AND THE LIMIT IS MECHANICAL, NOT CAUTIOUS: conflictWithActive, which ai:claim consults, refuses ANY overlap with an active task regardless of owner -- unlike ai:validate's error, which is scoped to different owners -- so the media-engine leaves these tasks genuinely share -- src/index.ts above all -- mean exactly one of this task, PL-0206 and PL-0205's successor PL-0207 can be active at a time. That was originally true of the packages/media-engine/** wildcard and it stayed true after the narrowing, because the overlap is real files rather than a wide prefix. It is a PATH fact and not a capacity one, and the distinction matters now: claude-media's maxParallel was raised from 1 to 2 in round 40, which changes nothing here because these three still share real files, and was done for PL-0601, whose surface is disjoint from all of them. PL-0205 went first because this task rests on it: failover.ts opens by saying this is where the three-way distinction PL-0205 established stops being bookkeeping and starts deciding things, and reviewing a consumer before the vocabulary it consumes is backwards. ONE THING FOR WHOEVER RECONCILES THIS: the performance gate cannot be recorded from npm run check. The single wall-clock assertion in failover.perf.test.ts is deselected BY NAME in packages/media-engine/vitest.config.ts unless vitest runs --mode bench, so a gate taken from the ordinary suite would describe the five deterministic read-count assertions and silently omit the timed one. Run npm run bench:failover in that workspace and record the gate from that, and only if it exits 0. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED FROM packages/media-engine/**, ON THE RULE THE REVIEWER STATED WHEN IT REFUSED PL-0205's WILDCARD: allowedPaths is write ownership, and keeping a wildcard solely because these tasks are already serialised is reservation inflation. The nine media-engine entries are the files this task actually wrote, read out of the implementation: failover.ts and scheduling.ts are the two halves of the policy, the four suites are its regressions, index.ts carries the one export line, vitest.config.ts exists ONLY for this task -- it deselects the wall-clock assertion by name so npm run check stays deterministic -- and package.json carries the ./scheduling export subpath and the bench:failover script, both created here. What is deliberately excluded is the rest of the package, which belongs to PL-0202, PL-0203 and PL-0207. ONE REVIEWDEPENDENCY ADDED, apps/web/src/components/player/playback-machine.ts. It is a CONSUMER rather than this task's work -- it imports scheduleAttempts from @liberty/media-engine/scheduling and schedules without ranking -- but the whole reason scheduling.ts exists as a separate module is that this consumer is a browser bundle edge, and failover.ts's header argues that at length. An approval that did not fingerprint the consumer would stay fresh after someone rewired it, which would silently invalidate the argument for the split. Read-only: this task does not write it, PL-0502 does. REFUSED ON THE MERITS AT 64b631d5, AND THE FINDING IS THAT A TEST WAS PROTECTING THE CLAUSE IT CONTRADICTED. boundedPolicy turned NaN into zero but deliberately left Infinity untouched, on the written argument that an infinite budget is a caller STATING a bound while only NaN is never anything a caller meant. gpt-architect refused that: an infinite budget is not a bound, it is the absence of one wearing a number's clothes. Both policy fields are ordinary numbers, so no cast is needed; attemptsUsed >= Infinity is false forever and count > Infinity is false forever, so under repeated transient failure neither the global nor the per-candidate condition ever terminates -- the unbounded reload loop pointed at a CDN that this module's own header says it exists to prevent, reached through the front door instead of through arithmetic. It directly contradicts the single acceptance clause, that retry and fallback behaviour is BOUNDED. THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING IS THE TEST. failover.test.ts pinned maxAttempts: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY as intended behaviour, with a comment restating the wrong argument. A regression suite agreeing with the code is not evidence that either is right, and this one was written to protect the clause it broke. THE FIX GENERALISES THE RULE RATHER THAN ADDING A CASE: boundedPolicy now delegates to an enforceableBudget helper that asks Number.isFinite, so the question is whether a number can bound anything at all rather than which exceptional values somebody thought of. Written as an allowlist for the same reason every other gate here is one -- NaN and the two infinities are the whole set today, but enumerating them would be a denylist over the numbers, and a denylist fails open on whatever it missed. A negative or zero budget is still passed through untouched, because that really is a caller stating a bound of nothing. Four regressions replace the one that was wrong: an infinite attempt budget, an infinite per-candidate retry budget, a NEGATIVE infinity that no enumeration of named values would have caught, and a finite budget passed through unchanged so the other three cannot pass by the guard simply zeroing everything. All three machine gates are re-recorded because the scheduler itself changed, including the bench performance gate, which the reviewer noted really had executed the timed test rather than inheriting the ordinary suite's exclusion. PROVENANCE WAS ACCEPTED, and separately the reviewer ruled on the shared introduction commit: this task and PL-0207 genuinely began in the same historical commit 4091a2b, a commit is not required to be task-atomic when recovering old history, and what matters is that the lower bound is truthful and the current review surface honest. No successor, no later base, no artificial path trimming -- record that the introduction commit is shared and leave it alone. THIS PARAGRAPH AND THE FOUR BEFORE IT SPENT TWO ROUNDS ON PL-0207'S RECORD BY MISTAKE, because the Edit anchors matched a nearly identical sentence there and neither edit was checked against the record it landed on. They are here now, and the mistake is recorded on PL-0207 rather than quietly erased. The lesson is small and general: an anchor that is unique in a diff is not necessarily unique in a file.

THE BASE WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN GUESSED, with planFailover and playbackAttemptFailureSchema as behaviour witnesses. The ordering check matters more here than anywhere else: this task spans a contract module and an engine module, so if the contract had landed first then the engine function's parent would sit INSIDE the implementation and the base would be narrowed exactly as PL-0205's was. The runner verified planFailover's introduction is at or before the contract's, took that commit's first parent, and confirmed neither witness appears in source at this base while both appear at HEAD. review.evidence: CHANGES_REQUESTED on the merits because the implementation deliberately preserves Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY as a policy budget while the task promises bounded retry and fallback; with infinite global attempts and infinite per-candidate transient retries, repeated transient failure has no terminating budget. Treat non-finite policy values in the same fail-closed direction already used for NaN, add regressions for both infinite fields, and refresh typecheck, unit and the dedicated bench performance gate. The rest of the failover policy is sound: rights, decode and unavailable-source findings are terminal, only network-transient is retryable, fresh candidates precede retries, charged unclassified attempts cannot silently reset the budget, the browser uses the shared scheduler, and reasons remain deterministic and observable. The historical window sharing its introduction commit and lower bound with PL-0207 is acceptable because one old commit carried both tasks and the current PL-0204 review surface, rather than commit exclusivity, defines what this approval will bind. recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Macrolanguage and extlang equivalence in the shared language matcher
recommended.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED BEFORE THIS TASK IS EVER CLAIMED, for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contains PL-0706's leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, so the wildcard would hold this P0 behind an unrelated security corrective for no benefit. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.
recommended.acceptance: The shared languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts stops reducing a tag to its primary subtag where that reduction crosses a MACROLANGUAGE boundary. A spoken-language distinction encompassed by a macrolanguage is not reported as a preferred-language fallback: zh-yue against zh-cmn, and either against a bare zh preference, must not answer with a fallback strength, because a fallback there tells the caller it may play Cantonese for a Mandarin preference. Canonical primary and extlang spellings of the SAME language are treated as equivalent in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one language -- and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix on either side. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers of the shared matcher, the audio track selection in audio.ts and the subtitle selection policy in subtitles.ts, rather than through the helper alone, so neither consumer can be corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. Any new outcome carries its own named reason: a distinction that is not regional must not be reported with a regional-fallback reason.

recommended.title: Corrective, re-run: auth integration decision, with a forgeable profile scope and an unsupported pin
recommended.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0401. It carries three merits blockers as well as a provenance correction, and the merits are the larger half. PROVENANCE: PL-0401 recorded implementationBaseSha fc1ea4d54c9e7d2b2f6d9aa71a977abdc3bcb400, proven with ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES. Those witnesses correctly located the code introduction and missed earlier task implementation on another declared write path: docs/DATA_MODEL.md did not exist at 56b343 and was created in bbe68ed8, before the recorded base, already identifying itself as covering this task's auth boundary and already selecting Better Auth 1.7.1. The true lower bound is 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7 while docs/DATA_MODEL.md remains a write surface. PL-0401 is BLOCKED with the false range preserved as audit history. DO NOT CLAIM THIS TASK UNTIL THE THREE BLOCKERS IN THE NOTES ARE IMPLEMENTED; it is created now so the findings are recorded against a task rather than living only in a review transcript.
recommended.notes: BLOCKER 1, AND IT IS THE PL-0706 DEFECT IN A SECOND PLACE. ProfileScope carries a type-only unique symbol property while mintProfileScope returns an ordinary object via cast, so a caller holding a genuine scope can write a spread with a replacement profileId and TypeScript carries the branded structural type straight through -- without the explicit cast ADR-007 claims is the only forgery route. Downstream persistence then trusts scope.profileId directly, which makes this a cross-profile data-access bypass rather than a typing nicety. The prescription: make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability rather than a compile-time proof, use issuance identity as well. The pattern already exists in this repository twice -- ClassifiedRuntime in packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and PinnedTarget in media-inspection -- module-private brand, freeze, WeakSet registry, identity check as the consumer's first action. BLOCKER 2, AND THE EXACT PIN IS WORKING RATHER THAN FAILING. better-auth and its Drizzle adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1. Upstream's current release is 1.7.4, from 2026-09-10, and its security policy supports only the latest version. The reviewer was explicit that this is not an argument against exact pins: it proves the policy works by making staleness visible, which is what ADR-007 said it was for. Move both packages together and update REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. DO NOT BUMP AND LEAVE THE MIGRATION: 1.7.3 restored the 1.6 account core schema after the issuer-schema change in 1.7.0 through 1.7.2, while this repository's hand-written migration still has an issuer column and an (issuer, account_id) uniqueness rule. The migration must be regenerated or reconciled against the reviewed version BEFORE security approval. That is why packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql moves from reviewDependency to WRITE PATH here: on PL-0401 it was only evidence, and read-only was correct; here it has to change, and reviewDependencies are read-only by contract. PL-0402 also owns packages/persistence and is BACKLOG, so no active conflict exists today, but the two must be sequenced and the reviewer should say which owns that file afterwards. BLOCKER 3. ADR-007 still states obsolete control-plane routing, naming gpt-architect as preferred implementer and claude-lead as reviewer, while the record now correctly has claude-backend implementing and gpt-architect reviewing independently. Rewrite that paragraph as history rather than as current routing, and prefer wording that points at the task gate as authoritative -- otherwise completing the review needs a post-approval edit that immediately stales the fingerprint it just bound. TWO HONEST CAVEATS CARRIED FORWARD FROM PL-0401, neither an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed, because no PostgreSQL exists in this environment, and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. SEQUENCING: this task is READY rather than BLOCKED because nothing external gates it, but it should not be claimed until the three blockers are implemented, and claiming it early would reserve packages/auth and two documents while no work was happening.
recommended.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range. The pinned version must be one upstream currently supports, and the hand-written migration must agree with that version's account schema rather than an abandoned intermediate one. ProfileScope must be UNFORGEABLE by a holder of a genuine scope: a spread copy carrying a replaced profileId must not remain assignable, and any consumer that grants data access on the strength of a scope must establish that the scope was ISSUED rather than merely that it type-checks. The decision record must describe the routing that actually applies, or point at the task record as authoritative rather than restating it.

recommended.title: A real catalog metadata source
recommended.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
recommended.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.

recommended.title: Corrective, re-run: channel and EPG contracts under an honest review range
recommended.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0601 and carries the same implementation forward under a base that covers the whole declared surface rather than only its code. PL-0601 recorded implementationBaseSha 33588cdce6de6a21c19a0f4725cc87b199deaa50, proven with two behaviour witnesses, liveChannelSchema and epgListingSchema, located by content pickaxe. Five checks passed and the answer was still wrong, for a reason no self-test could have caught: THE WITNESSES PROVED THE SCHEMA BOUNDARY, NOT THE TASK BOUNDARY. docs/LIVE_TV.md is an allowedPath and part of the stated implementation, and its PL-0601 rewrite -- the commit that replaced the original eleven-line Live TV note with the normalization-and-rights document -- landed at bbe68ed8d16f864c87309ceb1c089495deb89766, an ancestor of the recorded base. So the base tree already contained part of the implementation, and the published one-commit three-file window excluded task work it claimed to cover. THE TRUE BASE IS 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7, the parent of bbe68ed8, and it holds only while docs/LIVE_TV.md remains a write surface here -- which it should, because the documentation is half of what this task delivers. Claim this task, then start it with --reconcile-existing --base 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7. PL-0601 is BLOCKED with its false narrowed base preserved as audit history; it cannot be repaired in place, on the rule PL-0703 established.
recommended.notes: MERITS ALREADY APPROVED; PROVENANCE IS THE ONLY REASON THIS TASK EXISTS. gpt-architect read the implementation at 64b631d5 and said plainly that it saw no separate architecture or rights blocker behind the provenance defect: the channel requires a real shared rights basis, EPG listings structurally cannot carry playability, strict parsing refuses injected playability keys rather than stripping them, channel and listing mismatch produces a named refusal, and the documentation describes the same boundary accurately. It declined to record either review gate, because a verdict bound to a false range is worth less than no verdict. THE SIXTH STANDING CHECK CAME OUT OF THIS FAILURE and applies to every remaining reconciliation: after a behavioural base is proposed, inspect the history of EVERY allowedPath for task-attributable work predating it. ReviewDependencies may legitimately preexist and a write surface may contain unrelated older material, but any earlier delta that is itself part of the task means the candidate base is too late. In the reviewer's words, no self-test can compensate for asking the prover only about two symbols. The practical form: for each declared write path, list the commits touching it that are ancestors of the candidate base, and refuse the base if any is attributable to this task -- the cheapest mechanical signal being the task id in the commit message, with the remainder left for inspection rather than decided by the runner. SURFACE UNCHANGED FROM PL-0601, deliberately: packages/contracts/src/domains/live.ts, live.test.ts, module-boundary.test.ts -- whose retired assertion that src/domains/live.ts must NOT exist is this task's edit -- and docs/LIVE_TV.md. Dropping the document to shrink the window would be reservation inflation in reverse, and it is also what made the old base look defensible. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md stays out: this task defines contracts, not HTTP routes, and the reviewer confirmed the current API document is route-oriented rather than the owner of the live-domain schema. Those routes are PL-0602's, which is BLOCKED on licensed feed access. COLLISION-CHECKED: all four entries are leaf files, prefix-disjoint in both directions from PL-0204's contracts and media-engine leaves and from PL-0405's packages/auth and docs paths.
recommended.acceptance: Licensed channel, program, schedule and EPG contracts are typed and documented. A channel carries a REQUIRED, non-nullable rights basis drawn from the one shared vocabulary rather than a restated copy. No media address may appear in a channel or a listing, and that is structural rather than conventional: a playability-bearing-key list, a compile-time witness that the listing shape carries none of them, and strict parsing so a feed sending streamUrl is REFUSED rather than silently stripped. A listing cannot yield a rights basis on its own -- resolving one requires its channel, and a listing naming another channel produces a named refusal rather than null. Ordering over listings is deterministic and total, and an offset-less timestamp is refused rather than guessed. The documentation states what the contract does not cover, including that the opaque rights reference belongs to the provider layer rather than here.
